summary: A 60-foot steel fire tower on Thomas Mountain in the San Bernardino National Forest, built in the 1930s and scrapped in 1973; foundations and stonework remain.

facts.design: 60-ft Aermotor open X-brace steel tower with a 7x7 observation cabin on top, and a BC-201 residence cabin for the operator
facts.status_note: Cabin demolished and burned and tower dismantled and sold for scrap in 1973; the register says foundations, stone wall work and an access road remain.
facts.agency: US Forest Service - San Bernardino National Forest

events.note: Register and Wikipedia: 60-foot Aermotor steel tower with a 7x7 observation cabin and a BC-201 residence cabin
A ranger outpost and an AWS ground observer station stood nearby, 1936-45 (Hundred Peaks)
Hundred Peaks dates a 60-foot tower with a 7x7 metal cab to 1938; this conflicts with the 1935 date
Tower dismantled and sold for scrap after fire and vandalism; cabin demolished and burned

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Wikipedia give 1935; Hundred Peaks gives 1938 for a 60-foot tower with a 7x7 cab. None of the sources says whether the 1938 date marks a replacement tower
The register describes the residence cabin foundation, stone wall work and access road as remaining; Hundred Peaks says all except the foundation slabs are gone

notes_for_editor: Only three pages were read. The Forest Lookouts Thomas Mountain page has only a location line, so it is not cited. The geocache page for the site returned just its title when read, so it is not used. The 1935 and 1938 build dates conflict; the story reports both. No source describes current road or gate status. The brief has no height, so height_m 18.3 (60 ft) was added from the register and Hundred Peaks.
